cards.front: melting
cards.back: A solid changing to a liquid when it is heated.
cards.say: melting. A solid changing to a liquid when it is heated.

cards.front: freezing
cards.back: A liquid changing to a solid when it is cooled.
cards.say: freezing. A liquid changing to a solid when it is cooled.

cards.front: evaporation
cards.back: A liquid changing to a gas when it is heated.
cards.say: evaporation. A liquid changing to a gas when it is heated.

cards.front: condensation
cards.back: A gas changing to a liquid when it is cooled.
cards.say: condensation. A gas changing to a liquid when it is cooled.

cards.front: boiling
cards.back: When a liquid is heated until bubbles of gas form all through it.
cards.say: boiling. When a liquid is heated until bubbles of gas form all through it.

cards.front: At what temperature does water freeze?
cards.back: 0 degrees Celsius.
cards.say: At what temperature does water freeze? 0 degrees Celsius.

cards.front: At what temperature does water boil?
cards.back: 100 degrees Celsius.
cards.say: At what temperature does water boil? 100 degrees Celsius.

cards.front: At what temperature does ice melt?
cards.back: 0 degrees Celsius.
cards.say: At what temperature does ice melt? 0 degrees Celsius.

cards.front: What happens to ice in a warm room?
cards.back: It melts into water.
cards.say: What happens to ice in a warm room? It melts into water.

cards.front: What happens to water in a freezer?
cards.back: It freezes into ice.
cards.say: What happens to water in a freezer? It freezes into ice.

cards.front: Why does a puddle disappear on a hot day?
cards.back: The water evaporates into water vapour in the air.
cards.say: Why does a puddle disappear on a hot day? The water evaporates into water vapour in the air.

cards.front: What is water vapour?
cards.back: Water as a gas.
cards.say: What is water vapour? Water as a gas.

cards.front: Why does a cold glass get drops of water on the outside?
cards.back: Water vapour in the air cools on the glass and condenses.
cards.say: Why does a cold glass get drops of water on the outside? Water vapour in the air cools on the glass and condenses.

cards.front: Why does a bathroom mirror fog up after a hot shower?
cards.back: Warm vapour condenses on the cool mirror.
cards.say: Why does a bathroom mirror fog up after a hot shower? Warm vapour condenses on the cool mirror.

cards.front: What is the opposite of melting?
cards.back: Freezing.
cards.say: What is the opposite of melting? Freezing.

cards.front: What is the opposite of evaporation?
cards.back: Condensation.
cards.say: What is the opposite of evaporation? Condensation.

cards.front: Does chocolate melt in your hand?
cards.back: Yes. The warmth of your hand melts it.
cards.say: Does chocolate melt in your hand? Yes. The warmth of your hand melts it.

cards.front: What can you do to make washing dry faster?
cards.back: Hang it in the sun, because heat speeds up evaporation.
cards.say: What can you do to make washing dry faster? Hang it in the sun, because heat speeds up evaporation.

cards.front: Is evaporation faster in a warm place or a cold place?
cards.back: A warm place.
cards.say: Is evaporation faster in a warm place or a cold place? A warm place.

cards.front: What does a thermometer measure?
cards.back: Temperature.
cards.say: What does a thermometer measure? Temperature.

cards.front: In what unit do we measure temperature?
cards.back: Degrees Celsius.
cards.say: In what unit do we measure temperature? Degrees Celsius.

cards.front: What does a rising thermometer reading show?
cards.back: The temperature is getting higher.
cards.say: What does a rising thermometer reading show? The temperature is getting higher.

cards.front: True or false: Water can be a solid, liquid and gas.
cards.back: True. Ice, water and water vapour.
cards.say: True or false: Water can be a solid, liquid and gas. True. Ice, water and water vapour.

cards.front: How do clouds form?
cards.back: Water vapour rises, cools and condenses into tiny drops of water.
cards.say: How do clouds form? Water vapour rises, cools and condenses into tiny drops of water.

cards.front: True or false: Boiling and evaporation are the same.
cards.back: False. Evaporation happens slowly from the surface at any temperature, boiling is when bubbles form through the liquid.
cards.say: True or false: Boiling and evaporation are the same. False. Evaporation happens slowly from the surface at any temperature, boiling is when bubbles form through the liquid.
